To digest the required docs it dispatched several **`scout`** sub-agents in parallel (10:43:34): one to read `extensions.md`, one for `skills.md`, one for `packages.md`. A second batch (10:43:50) scouted `sdk.play.date` and the `pi-utils-settings` README. The Playdate SDK web docs were unreachable from `scout` (`sdk.play.date` timed out), and the agent dispatched two more scout calls (10:44:19, 10:53:48–10:54:34) attempting to get starter `main.lua`, `main.c`, `CMakeLists.txt`, and `pdxinfo` templates.

A `worker` subagent (10:46:00 — codex) was dispatched to fix `optionArgs` shape and `ToolFooter` in `src/tools/doctor.ts`.

The user redirected several times in this phase:
- 10:43 "for the skill, make sure to confirm by reading the docs too"
- 10:49 "just use typebox only" / "use latest version of pi-utils-ui too"
- 10:51 told the agent that `promptGuidelines` strings need to mention the tool name (because they're concatenated into the system prompt with no context), and asked to drop the `playdate_new_project` tool, making scaffolding skill-driven.
- 10:53 "where did you get the templates from?" — the agent had been guessing from search results.
- 10:55 "the sdk is installed locally, does it include the docs?" pointing to `https://sdk.play.date/3.0.5/Inside%20Playdate.html` and other URLs.

The agent located the local SDK at `~/Developer/PlaydateSDK` (version 3.0.5), confirmed `Inside Playdate.html` and `Inside Playdate with C.html` plus `Examples/Game Template`, `C_API/Examples/Hello World`, and started reading them via grep/Read.

Pending: verify templates against SDK, finish typecheck, finish remaining reference files, generate `schema.json`, write README. "Blocked: SDK docs site times out."

## Phase 3 — Repo creation and first round of tool-failure debugging (11:04–11:09)

The user asked the agent to (11:04) "create the git repo, private for now" and (11:06) configure it like other extensions (description, CI/CD, disable wiki, disable merge commits, etc.). The agent created `github.com/aliou/pi-playdate` (private), set repo settings via `gh`, and pushed `9ef2f23` "initial extension".

At **11:09:04** the user told the agent to *read another session log* — a separate pi session at `/Users/alioudiallo/.pi/agent/sessions/--Users-alioudiallo-code-src-github.com-aliou-playdate-games--/2026-04-15T11-03-48-401Z_…jsonl` — where the freshly-installed extension was failing, and asked it to also figure out how to control the simulator from the SDK.

- `playdate_build`: false negative `"Build failed with 0 error(s)."` when `pdc` exits non-zero but parses no diagnostics.
- `playdate_run_sim`: PID/process confusion (macOS `open -a` launches a short-lived launcher process).

It then ran an **`oracle`** call (11:11:39) to think through the four issues and dispatched four parallel `worker` subagents (codex) (11:13:57–11:14:48) to fix each in `lib/sim.ts` (direct binary launch), `lib/pdc.ts` (synthetic fallback diagnostic on non-zero exit), `tools/screenshot.ts` (skip PID check on macOS), `tools/build.ts` (better message), and `tools/sim_log.ts` (helpful empty-buffer message).

## Phase 4 — Screenshot and input via osascript; user pivots to DAP (11:20–11:32)

User (11:20:27): "regarding screenshot and controlling the simulator, is there anything in the SDK that helps with that? right now neither work." The agent tried two macOS approaches: an `osascript` window-id lookup (returned `missing value`), then was patched (11:23:24, codex worker) to use a Swift/CoreGraphics `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` snippet driving `screencapture -l`.

User (11:23:06): "read the screenshot?" — testing it.

User (11:27:03) pointed at `help.play.date/developer/dev-links/` and asked the agent to probe what the simulator exposes. The agent fetched the page (11:27:08), then ran scout calls into `midouest/vscode-playdate-debug` (11:27:57) and (11:32:53) about the simulator's built-in DAP server on TCP `:55934`.

User (11:32:38) reported having two simulator instances open, closed both, and pointed the agent at the `tictactoe` game. The agent re-probed and discovered the simulator's DAP support documented in `Inside Playdate.html` near "Advanced Debugging".

## Phase 5 — DAP integration (11:39–11:53)

User (11:39:58) said: write a real DAP client into the extension, then use it; ask whether the connection needs to be persistent. The agent established that DAP runs on TCP `localhost:55934`, uses `Content-Length: N\r\n\r\nJSON` framing (LSP-style), and supports REPL commands (`help`, `p`, `eval`, `s`, `n`, `r`, `c`). It verified concrete probes:
- `eval print("HELLO_FROM_DAP")`
- `p playdate.display.getWidth()` → `400`
- `eval playdate.simulator.writeToFile(playdate.graphics.getDisplayImage(), "/tmp/pd-dap-screenshot.png")` produced a clean 400×240 PNG
- `playdate.AButtonDown()`, `playdate.rightButtonDown()`, etc. directly trigger the game's Lua callbacks

User (11:42–11:43) noted that game state in Lua locals can't be read, suggested adding an `inspect` module + `getState()` pattern, and asked whether to vendor it or have the extension inject it. The agent decided the extension would auto-inject a `__pd_inspect()` Lua table-serializer on each DAP connect.

User (11:43:50): "make the worker implement it." A `worker` subagent (11:44:35) was dispatched to create `src/lib/dap.ts` (~200 lines: TCP socket, framing, sequence numbers, pending-request tracking with 10s timeout, dedup via `connectPromise`, `evaluate()`, `evalLua()`, `printExpr()`, `screenshot()` methods, AbortSignal threaded through, `__pd_inspect()` injection). Three more workers (11:45:47–11:48:19) wired `DapClient` into `state.ts`/`sim.ts`, rewrote `screenshot.ts` to use DAP first (with osascript fallback), rewrote `sim_input.ts` similarly, and created a new `sim_eval.ts` tool.

User (11:49:54) "update the skills too?" and (11:50:16) "probably drop the fallback using osascript, not reliable enough tbh."

At **11:53:19** the harness compacted again. The summary marks `dap.ts`, `sim_eval.ts` done, `screenshot.ts`/`sim_input.ts` switched to DAP-only (osascript fallback removed), simulator launched via the real binary not `open -a`, `pdc` synthetic fallback diagnostics added. User (11:53:19): "abstract away the dap client, the agent shouldn't have to run anything, just running a command should do the work… make sure that the signal is used though, it seems like you skip it." User (11:58–11:59) asked whether SKILL.md and `promptGuidelines` explain the buttons so an agent can self-play, then (11:59:31) re-reminded the agent that "the prompt guideline must include the name of the tool or be a single string, they're dropped without tool context otherwise." ## Phase 7 — Restart/log/state diagnostics (13:09–13:33)

The next user message lands ~70 minutes later. User (13:09:19): "are there tools to restart the simulator / rebuild?" (13:10:20): "regarding logging, is there a file we could have be polled automatically, similar to … pi-processes log watchers?" (13:17:02): "look at the vscode extension we saw earlier… how does it handle this? https://help.play.date/developer/dev-links/ … list out what the extension does that we don't."

The agent fetched the dev-links page, scouted `midouest/vscode-playdate-debug` (13:17:09) for comparison. It catalogued features (DAP proxy with 7 protocol fixers, `waitForDebugPort` retry loop, `incrementBuildNumber`), noted what pi-playdate has that vscode-playdate-debug doesn't (DAP screenshots, DAP button input, eval, inspect injection, doctor, C/CMake, device deploy).

## Phase 8 — Stuck simulators, build/stop race, clean-build bug (13:33–14:02)

User (13:33:33): "i have 7 simulators running currently, probably from [earlier session]. why aren't they reusing the same? the tools are not correctly re-using the open simulator."  
User (13:34:26): "but why? can it not re-use the simulator?"  
User (13:36:55): "yes."

User (13:43:43) pointed the agent at the same `playdate-games` session log: "After reloading the extension and after telling the agent that the simulator wasn't running, it started the simulator and then tried to input A. Then the simulator seemed to have crashed."  
User (13:44:00): "look at the end of the session. just look at the file yourself please."  
User (13:45:14): "are the dap errors returned to the agent? in the ui, only seeing `DAP connection closed`."  
User (13:46:07): "wait if it's in the session it was returned to the agent. so just add it to the tool renderResult in addition to the `DAP connection closed`."

User (13:53:27): "explain this error: `Playdate Build ./tictactoe target=simulator clean=true → Build failed. 1: Couldn't create folder at tictactoe/tictactoe.pdx`. also … why did it struggle to find the simulator pid?"

The agent diagnosed: the agent had called `playdate_build(clean: true)` while the simulator still had the `.pdx` open, so `pdc` couldn't recreate the bundle directory. It proposed fixing `killSimulator` to use `SIGKILL` (because the stuck sim ignored `SIGTERM`) and auto-killing the sim when `clean: true`.

User (13:54:36): "are you sure about that locking the bundle ???" The agent retracted ("No, I'm not sure. Let me check what actually happens.") and re-read `tools/build.ts`, `lib/pdc.ts`, `lib/project.ts`.

1. Reuse only when DAP is reachable; otherwise kill and respawn.
2. `killSimulator` uses `SIGKILL` / `pkill -9`.
3. `playdate_build(clean: true)` auto-kills the sim first.

User (14:02:04): "Okay, now we have another issue. Running multiple times the button tap might not work as expected because tool calls are done in parallel and not sequentially by default… 1. add a new tool that allows multiple taps at once… 2. force tool calls to be sequential using `withFileMutationQueue` with a dummy file."

The agent grepped `pi-mono` for `withFileMutationQueue`, read its implementation (per-key promise chain), confirmed it's re-exported, and used **`AskUserQuestion`** to confirm Option 2 (sentinel queue). User chose "Queue only".

User (14:11:33): "any updates to do to the documentation anywhere?" The agent updated `AGENTS.md` and `SKILL.md`, but user (14:12:44) said "i don't think the skill update is needed tbh", so the agent reverted that part of `SKILL.md` and amended/force-pushed.

User (14:13:40): "now let's rewrite the git history: put everything in a single commit. it might be easier to delete the .git and then git init and git commit and re-add the remote and force push on it."

The agent ran `rm -rf .git && git init && git add . && git commit -m "feat: pi-playdate extension for Playdate game development…"` then `git remote add origin … && git push --force` (force-pushed `8ba91d1`, 51 files, 9,411 insertions). ## Phase 11 — Menu / lock / crank / accelerometer investigation (14:56–15:00)

After a ~40-minute gap, user (14:56:25): "is it possible to have tools to trigger: the menu, the lock, the crank, the accelerator". Model is `claude-opus-4-6` again.

The agent grep-searched the local SDK for `simulator.`, `accelerometer|accelerator`, `crank`, `setMenu|addMenu|menu item|lock` and concluded **mostly "no"**:
- "menu" — not real; current `playdate_sim_input.menu` is just a hack toggling `playdate.setAutoLockDisabled`
- "lock" — probably no
- "crank" — not properly
- "accelerometer" — same

User (14:57:28): "but wait how are we able to input but not crank? that makes no sense." The agent explained the distinction (buttons have Lua callbacks like `playdate.AButtonDown()` so DAP can fire them; crank/accelerometer are queried each frame from the engine, no callback to spoof).

User (14:58:20): "are you sure? yes look for more stuff and figure it out. go through the sdk code or whatever, look at the other extensions / integration etc."

The agent fetched `help.play.date/developer/dev-links/` (got HTTP 429 — rate-limited), dispatched two scouts (one search, one to `midouest/vscode-playdate-debug`). Both scout calls reported partial failures (`github_content`: `Authentication failed. Check SCOUT_GITHUB_TOKEN validity.`, `github_search`: same). The agent then grepped local SDK for `AButtonDown|cranked|getCrankPosition|readAccelerometer`, ran `strings -a` + grep on `Playdate Simulator.app/Contents/MacOS/Playdate Simulator`, and found:

- Internal command-string formats: `changecrank %f`, `dockcrank 0`, `dockcrank 1`, `accel %i %i %i`, `autolock`, `setAutoLock`, `setAutoLockDisabled`
- Menu labels: `&Control Device with Simulator`, `&Use Device As Controller`
- Symbols: `DebugAdapter*`, `DebuggerConnectionThread*`, `_pc_setAutoLockDisabled`, `_pc_system_getAutoLock`, `_pc_system_setAutoLock`, `_pd_setAutoLockMode`, etc.

The agent ran one more synthetic_web_search for `"changecrank" Playdate Simulator accel dockcrank` (returned only the public simulator manual). Then produced its final message:

> "Yep. I changed my mind a bit. … the simulator binary contains `changecrank %f`, `dockcrank 0/1`, `accel %i %i %i`, `autolock`, `setAutoLock`, `setAutoLockDisabled` … strong evidence the simulator has a real internal control path … I have **not** yet found the exact programmable channel for those hidden commands. … So I would not say 'we can implement it immediately' yet. I would say 'it is very likely implementable.' … If you want, next step I can do is: 1. find the actual transport for `changecrank`/`accel`, or 2. implement documented keyboard-based menu/lock/crank support first."

The session ends here at **15:00:59 UTC**, mid-investigation, with the agent waiting for direction on which option to take. There is no resolution to the menu/lock/crank/accelerometer feature request. Throughout the session 27 tool results returned errors (TS compile errors, `Could not find edits[0]`, `HTTP 429`, scout auth failures, build false-negatives). The extension itself was repeatedly: scaffolded → broken when used in a sibling pi session → debugged from that session's log → patched → committed → repeated; final published state is single commit `8ba91d1` on `github.com/aliou/pi-playdate`, with `playdate_doctor`, `playdate_build`, `playdate_run_sim`, `playdate_stop_sim`, `playdate_sim_log`, `playdate_screenshot`, `playdate_sim_input`, `playdate_sim_eval`, `playdate_run_device` tools registered, DAP-only for Lua control, sentinel-queue serialization on DAP tools.
